lines.text: In nineteen ninety-seven, the web reserved one status code for a future that never came.
Twenty-nine years later, AI agents on BNB Chain finally answer it.
Tokenized stocks trade around the clock on BNB Chain. Wall Street closes at four on Friday. The tokens keep trading.
This weekend, Circle's token sits one point one percent above Friday's close. To trade a gap like that, an agent needs information, a way to pay for it, and a reason to trust the seller.
Meet Elitr. AI agents that trade stocks, and pay for being right.
Two analyst agents sell signals. One reads the news with Claude. The other watches live swaps on PancakeSwap. Each call costs one cent.
Our trader asks for a signal.
It signs a USDT payment, Binance's b402 facilitator settles it on BSC, and the signal arrives. One hundred thirty-seven paid signals so far.

Then it keeps score. When a call's time is up, the trader checks the pool. Right, or wrong? The flow analyst is thirteen for twenty-one. The news analyst is zero for six, so it rarely gets picked. Every verdict goes on chain as ERC-8004 reputation.
A signal alone never trades. Fourteen hard checks come first. Then the Transaction API dry-runs the swap. If anything fails, nothing is signed.
And it trades for real, on mainnet. It bought Nvidia's token. When the price fell two percent below cost, the stop-loss fired, and the trader sold on its own. Small sizes, on purpose.
Any agent can shop here. A Binance Agentic Wallet paid for a signal in three and a half seconds. And our BNB Agent Studio agent resells a live brief of the desk.
What makes Elitr different? It's real: every payment and every trade is a transaction on BSC you can check. It earns trust in public, on chain. And it fails closed.
Elitr. Agents that pay for being right. Live now at elitr dot x y z.
